```{=html}
    <h1>The neutral pion</h1>
  </header>
```

::: {.qft-exam-body}
In $e^+e^-$ collisions one can observe collisions of almost real photons emitted by the electrons and positrons at small angles to the beam axis. In such collisions the photons can produce a neutral pion. The cross section of this reaction is proportional to the decay width $\Gamma(\pi^0\to\gamma\gamma)$ and provides a way to measure it.

\(i\) Compute the cross section of the reaction $\gamma+\gamma\to\pi^0$ in QED: $$\sigma(\gamma+\gamma\to\pi^0) = \frac{8\pi^2\,\Gamma(\pi^0\to\gamma\gamma)}{m_\pi}\,\delta\bigl((p+k)^2-m_\pi^2\bigr),$$ where $p,k$ are the 4-momenta of the photons (Low's formula; the photons are unpolarized).

\(ii\) Check that the matrix element of the reaction $\gamma+\gamma\to\pi^0$ is nonzero only when the helicities of the photons are equal (for linear polarizations, when they are mutually perpendicular).

\(iii\) Check that in the decay $\pi^0\to\gamma\gamma$ the combination $(\boldsymbol{E}_1+\boldsymbol{E}_2)\cdot (\boldsymbol{B}_1+\boldsymbol{B}_2)$ is nonzero only for the same photon polarizations.

:::
